images.heading: My Key Priorities
images.nearby: Workforce Readiness & Career Pathways Our students shouldn't have to leave San Jose to find opportunity. I will expand career and technical education, build real pipelines to local businesses, and make sure every graduate walks out with more than a diploma. Learn More

images.heading: My Key Priorities
images.nearby: Fiscal Accountability & Transparency I have managed multi-million-dollar operations across multiple Wingstop locations and multiple businesses. I know how to read a budget, ask the hard questions to ensure every dollar works for students — not disappear into overhead. Learn More

images.heading: My Key Priorities
images.nearby: Special Needs & Inclusive Education My son Andy was diagnosed with autism at age 2.5. That experience changed everything — and it's why I founded Andy's Cafe, serve on the Parents Helping Parents board, and fight every day to ensure students with special needs have the support, resources, and futures they deserve. Learn More

images.heading: My Key Priorities
images.nearby: Community Partnerships & Economic Opportunity East San Jose has an incredible community. I will make sure the district is tapping into it — through local business partnerships, mentorship programs, and parent engagement that actually reaches the families who need it most. Learn More

images.heading: My Unique Perspective
images.nearby: Entrepreneurial Leadership Built and scaled businesses from the ground up, with strengths in strategy, financial management, and team leadership—bringing a results-driven mindset to school governance.

images.heading: My Unique Perspective
images.nearby: Strategic Decision-Making Experienced in long-term planning, innovation, and stakeholder communication to support sustainable growth and responsible district leadership.

images.heading: My Unique Perspective
images.nearby: Harvard YALP Training Completed Harvard Business School’s Young American Leaders Program (2023), focused on public-sector leadership, data-driven decisions, and ethical governance.

images.heading: My Unique Perspective
images.nearby: Economic Development Advisor Served on San Jose’s Small Business Advisory Board, supporting local growth, shaping policy, and strengthening public-private collaboration.

images.heading: My Unique Perspective
images.nearby: Nonprofit Board Leadership Board member at Parents Helping Parents, contributing to governance, program oversight, fundraising, and advocacy for families with special needs.

images.heading: My Unique Perspective
images.nearby: Special Education Advocate Hands-on experience navigating IEPs, supporting families, and advocating for inclusive education systems that better serve students with diverse needs.

images.heading: My Unique Perspective
images.nearby: ESTA: Representing 1,200 Teachers Across ESUHSD "The East Side Teachers Association is proud to endorse Tony Lam for the ESUHSD Board of Trustees, Area 4. Tony's commitment to supporting teachers, expanding career pathways for students, and advocating for special needs resources aligns perfectly with our mission to ensure every student in our district has the opportunity to succeed. As both a parent in the district and a proven business leader, Tony brings the perspective and experience we need on the board. ESTA stands behind Tony Lam because he stands with our teachers and our students." – East Side Teachers Association Executive Board – East Side Teachers Association Executive Board

About Me
## Why I'm Running
I am a San Jose entrepreneur, nonprofit founder, and father who has spent my career creating opportunities for people others overlook. As a first-generation American raised in East San Jose and the father of a son with autism, I know firsthand what's at stake when our schools fall short — and what's possible when they rise to the challenge. I'm running for the ESUHSD Board of Trustees because every student in East San Jose deserves a school system that believes in them as much as I do.
The Platform
## My Key Priorities
Workforce Readiness & Career Pathways
Our students shouldn't have to leave San Jose to find opportunity. I will expand career and technical education, build real pipelines to local businesses, and make sure every graduate walks out with more than a diploma.
Learn More
Fiscal Accountability & Transparency
I have managed multi-million-dollar operations across multiple Wingstop locations and multiple businesses. I know how to read a budget, ask the hard questions to ensure every dollar works for students — not disappear into overhead.
Learn More
Special Needs & Inclusive Education
My son Andy was diagnosed with autism at age 2.5. That experience changed everything — and it's why I founded Andy's Cafe, serve on the Parents Helping Parents board, and fight every day to ensure students with special needs have the support, resources, and futures they deserve.
Learn More
Community Partnerships & Economic Opportunity

Qualifications
## My Unique Perspective
I bring the strategic thinking of a business leader, the training of an executive education graduate, the governance experience of a board member, and the heart of a parent advocate. This combination is exactly what our schools need right now.
Entrepreneurial Leadership
Built and scaled businesses from the ground up, with strengths in strategy, financial management, and team leadership—bringing a results-driven mindset to school governance.
Strategic Decision-Making
Experienced in long-term planning, innovation, and stakeholder communication to support sustainable growth and responsible district leadership.
Harvard YALP Training
Completed Harvard Business School’s Young American Leaders Program (2023), focused on public-sector leadership, data-driven decisions, and ethical governance.
Economic Development Advisor
Served on San Jose’s Small Business Advisory Board, supporting local growth, shaping policy, and strengthening public-private collaboration.
Nonprofit Board Leadership
Board member at Parents Helping Parents, contributing to governance, program oversight, fundraising, and advocacy for families with special needs.
Special Education Advocate
Hands-on experience navigating IEPs, supporting families, and advocating for inclusive education systems that better serve students with diverse needs.

page.text:
Key Priorities
## Special Needs & Inclusive Education
This one is personal. My son Andy was diagnosed with autism at age 2.5. From that moment on, my family and I became students of a different kind of system — one full of IEP meetings, evaluations, therapy waitlists, and the constant work of advocating for a child who deserves every opportunity. Andy is now 12 years old and making remarkable progress. But I know that progress didn't happen by accident. It happened because my family had the resources, the knowledge, and the persistence to fight for it. Not every family does. And that has to change.
#### Personal Connection
I don't just talk about special needs education — I live it. I serve on the board of Parents Helping Parents, an organization that supports over 6,000 families a year with children with special needs across the US. I founded Andy's Cafe, a nonprofit coffee shop that employs adults from the autism and special needs community, specifically because I read that 85% of autistic adults with college degrees are unemployed. That statistic stopped me cold. And it drove me to build something that proves the world wrong.
As both a parent of a special needs child and a father of a son currently attending Piedmont Hills High School in the district, I bring unique perspectives on inclusive education and the everyday challenges our students face.
The Problem
Special needs students are often underserved and under-resourced
IEP processes can feel confusing and adversarial for families
Transition-to-adulthood planning is inconsistent or lacking
Inclusive classroom practices vary widely across schools
Families who need the most support often have the least access to it
My Approach
I will bring to the board something most board members don't have:
Lived experience as a special needs parent
Professional experience running an organization that employs adults with autism
A network of advocates, service providers, and community organizations already doing this work
I will be a voice for these students and families at every budget meeting, every policy discussion, and every strategic planning session.
## My Proposals
1. IEP Advocacy and Family Support
2. Autism Support Programs
3. Transition-to-Adulthood Planning
4. Inclusive Classrooms
Andy's Cafe exists because I refused to accept that the system couldn't do better. I'm bringing that same refusal to the ESUHSD board. Every student with a disability in this district deserves a future — and I will fight to make sure the district is building one for them.
